title: The "450 civilians" accusation on Núi Bà Đen
displayDate: Late August 1965 (inferred — days before the medevac)
description: On a day when Sgt. Lowry was the only Special Forces man at the mountain camp — call sign Body Jab 42 — a helicopter radioed Larry directly (his search-and-rescue call sign was Tay Ninh) that hundreds of enemy were digging fighting positions outside the perimeter. Larry ran around the French fort to relay the warning to Lowry. About half an hour later Lowry came running back shouting that Larry had "killed 450 civilians down there," then ran off. Larry never saw what happened. Sensing something was wrong, he radioed headquarters at Tân Sơn Nhứt and called for Rosethorn 007 — his command's helicopter — which came for him within about an hour. He places this at the very end of his tour: back at Tân Sơn Nhứt a medic diagnosed yellow jaundice, and he was medevaced out a couple of days later.
larrysRecollection: "You son of a bitch! You killed 450 civilians down there" — Lowry's words as Larry remembers them. "Wherever down there was, I never saw any of this... I immediately thought something was not kosher." Larry adds that he later heard a mass grave of 450 civilians was found at the base of the mountain after the war, and says he wonders whether he was set up as a scapegoat.
researchNotes: Told in full for the first time in Tell a Story comments on 2026-08-13 (data/recollections/giscus-stories-c18006791.json, -c18006833.json, and -c18006851.json). The date is inferred: he ties the incident to the end of his service and the medevac "a couple days later," and he arrived in Japan around early September 1965. No documentation has yet been sought for the accusation, for any strike or civilian-casualty incident near the mountain in this window, or for the post-war mass-grave account — research plan in research/events/450-civilians-nui-ba-den.md.
